phase: 1B - deterministic existing-credential authentication and actor validation
objective: Authenticate exactly one existing user, project, or internal-service credential per request; fail closed on malformed or conflicting credentials; and strictly validate durable user and project actors. Organization credential persistence, authentication, and actor success are deferred to Phase 1C.
verified_facts: User principles expose a durable user actor using the user ID.
ProjectScope exposes a durable project actor using project_credentials.id rather than project ID.
ServiceScope carries delegated authorization context and deliberately has no external audit actor.
OrganizationScope currently has organization context but no credential ID, local web resolver, persistence entity, or durable actor.
User, project, and service middleware independently write the same context key and currently rely on interceptor order when multiple credentials are supplied.
Current middleware commonly logs malformed credentials and continues without authentication.
Integration API installs project and service authentication but not user authentication.
The user streaming interceptor incorrectly requires x-project-id even though a user can be authenticated without selecting a project.

user.presence: Present when any of authorization, x-auth-id, or x-project-id is non-blank.
user.validity: authorization and x-auth-id are required; x-auth-id must be a non-zero uint64; x-project-id is optional and, when present, must be a non-zero uint64 authorized by the user principle.
user.gin_precedence: Preserve current compatibility order: authorization path parameter, then header, then query; x-auth-id header, then path parameter, then query; x-project-id header, then path parameter, then query.

project.validity: Trim surrounding whitespace; remove rpd-prj- only when it is the leading prefix; the remaining key must be non-blank and the project authenticator must accept it.
project.gin_precedence: Preserve current compatibility order: header, then query, then path parameter.

service.validity: The signed service assertion must validate and contain a normalized delegated organization context; project and user context remain optional.
service.gin_sources: Not public and not added in this phase.

conflict_contract.rule: If more than one credential class is present, reject before invoking any authenticator or business handler.
conflict_contract.same_class_sources: Existing source precedence remains compatible in this phase; duplicate same-class values are not treated as cross-class conflicts.

failure_contract.no_credential: Continue without authentication so existing public and health routes remain compatible; authenticated handlers reject through their existing checks.
failure_contract.grpc_malformed_or_conflicting: Return codes.Unauthenticated with a stable generic message and do not invoke the downstream handler.
failure_contract.grpc_resolver_rejection: Return codes.Unauthenticated with a stable generic message and do not invoke the downstream handler.
failure_contract.gin_malformed_or_conflicting: Abort with HTTP 401 and the existing generic authentication error response helper where available; never include credential contents.
failure_contract.gin_resolver_rejection: Abort with HTTP 401 and do not invoke downstream handlers.
failure_contract.logging: Log credential class and failure category only; never log raw tokens, keys, or signed assertions.

acceptance_criteria: A request presenting more than one user, project, or service credential class is rejected before business logic.
A presented but malformed or rejected credential fails authentication instead of silently falling through.
No-credential requests preserve existing unauthenticated pass-through behavior.
Unary gRPC, streaming gRPC, and existing Gin user/project middleware apply the same presence, conflict, and failure semantics.
The user streaming interceptor accepts a valid user credential without x-project-id.
Integration API installs user authentication with the same ordering and conflict contract as endpoint and assistant APIs.
ResolveAuditActor returns ActorTypeUser with user ID for user principles.
ResolveAuditActor returns ActorTypeProject with project_credentials.id for ProjectScope.
ResolveAuditActor rejects an actor type that does not match AuthenticationPrinciple.Type().
ServiceScope remains actorless delegated context and is excluded from external actor resolution.
OrganizationScope remains actorless and organization authentication is not wired in this phase.
Existing valid user, project, and service requests retain their successful behavior.

implementation_slices.name: credential selection
changes: Add shared request credential-presence classification for gRPC metadata and existing Gin sources.
Add unary and streaming conflict interceptors before concrete authenticators.
Add Gin conflict middleware before user/project authenticators.
Reject all cross-class pairs including service plus external credentials.

implementation_slices.name: fail-closed authenticators
changes: Change user, project, and service middleware so malformed or rejected presented credentials terminate authentication.
Make user project selection optional and consistent in unary, stream, and Gin.
Normalize project credential prefix removal to leading-prefix behavior.

implementation_slices.name: strict existing actors
changes: Validate that ActorIdentity.Type matches AuthenticationPrinciple.Type() for user and project principles.
Reject organization and service principles from external actor resolution until their durable identities are implemented.
Retain project credential ID validation in web scoped authentication and project authenticator.

implementation_slices.name: transport parity
changes: Wire user authentication into integration unary and stream servers.
Wire conflict middleware into endpoint, integration, assistant, and web gRPC chains.
Wire conflict middleware into assistant Gin routes that already install user/project authentication.
Add explicit wiring-order tests rather than relying only on command compilation.

out_of_scope_behavior: Organization credential persistence, local web resolution, transport wiring, management APIs, archival, or rotation.
Organization actor success or substituting organization ID as actor ID.
Service actor identity or originating-actor propagation through service JWTs.
Migrating created_by or updated_by persistence fields.
Treating project ID, organization ID, raw keys, or token fingerprints as actor IDs.

principles.kiss: Add one credential classifier and reuse existing concrete authenticators rather than replacing them.
principles.yagni: Do not create organization credential or service actor infrastructure in this slice.
principles.single_ownership: The classifier owns cross-class conflict decisions; concrete middleware owns validation of its credential class.
principles.single_source_of_truth: ResolveAuditActor remains the actor normalization boundary and validates authentication-type parity.
principles.contracts: Credential presence, validity, failure response, actor identity, and authorization context are explicit and separate.
principles.fail_safe: Malformed, conflicting, rejected, actorless, or mismatched credentials fail before business logic.
principles.observability: Authentication logs contain class and category but no credential material.
principles.least_privilege: No new credential class gains business authorization in this slice.
principles.reversibility: The slice is code-only and can be reverted without schema, protobuf, or data rollback.

required_tests: credential classifier accepts each single user, project, and service class
credential classifier rejects all three cross-class pairs
invalid user, project, and service credentials do not invoke downstream handlers
no-credential requests invoke downstream handlers without authentication
user unary and stream authentication work without x-project-id
project prefix normalization only removes a leading prefix
Gin and gRPC conflict behavior parity
organization and service actor resolution failure
command wiring tests assert interceptor presence and order for endpoint, integration, assistant, and web
risks: Clients that accidentally send multiple credential classes will begin receiving explicit authentication failures.
Malformed credentials that previously fell through may now fail earlier with a different transport-level error.
Gin response helpers differ across binaries, so tests must pin the actual 401 contract.
Interceptor order must place conflict detection before all credential-specific authenticators.
No-credential pass-through must remain intact for public routes.
rollback: Revert credential classification, fail-closed middleware behavior, actor-type parity validation, integration user wiring, and command wiring together. Existing serialized credentials and persisted data remain unchanged.
